_comment: Block/item/mob/biome of the day. Facts verified against minecraft.wiki (current Java Edition) at write time; since_version is the Java version named on that page's History.

entries.name: Crafting Table
facts: Two damaged same-material items in the grid merge durability plus a 5% bonus.
Grid repairs strip enchantments from the items.
It can generate in a hidden room of trial chambers.
entries.tip: Repair enchanted gear on an anvil, not in the grid, to keep its enchantments.

entries.name: Furnace
facts: It smelts one item every 200 ticks, or 10 seconds.
An active furnace gives off light level 13.
Fuel keeps burning even after the input runs out.
entries.tip: A coal lump smelts 8 items, so load full stacks to avoid wasting fuel.

entries.name: Bookshelf
facts: Breaking one drops three books.
Fifteen nearby bookshelves unlock level 30 enchantments.
A bookshelf works as furnace fuel for 1.5 items.
entries.tip: Use an axe to break it fast, or Silk Touch to keep the bookshelf block.

entries.name: TNT
facts: Primed TNT usually explodes after 80 ticks, which is 4 seconds.
Its default explosion power is 4.
Primed TNT can travel through Nether portals, fuse intact.
entries.tip: TNT usually cannot destroy blocks underwater.

entries.name: Obsidian
facts: Only diamond or netherite pickaxes can mine it.
Its blast resistance is 1,200, so normal explosions spare it.
The wither is the only mob that can break it.
entries.tip: Breaking an ender chest without Silk Touch drops 8 obsidian.

entries.name: Anvil
facts: A placed anvil cannot be moved by pistons.
Item names typed at an anvil can be up to 50 characters.
Anvil sounds got slightly quieter in 1.21.11.
entries.tip: An iron ingot or diamond repairs 25% of an item's maximum durability.

entries.name: Beacon
facts: Its beam reaches 2048 blocks high since 1.21.5.
Effect range is 20, 30, 40 or 50 blocks by pyramid level.
Effects last roughly 11 to 17 seconds per refresh.
entries.tip: Build a level 4 pyramid to unlock Regeneration and a level II primary power.

entries.name: Enchanting Table
facts: It gives off light level 7.
Pistons cannot push it, and sticky pistons cannot pull it.
Fifteen bookshelves around it enable level 30 enchantments.
entries.tip: Leave one block of gap between each bookshelf and the table.

entries.name: Lodestone
facts: Pistons cannot push or pull it.
Since 1.21.5 it is crafted with an iron ingot, not netherite.
Since 1.21.5 it can appear in chests of ruined portals.
entries.tip: Since 1.21.5 lodestones are renewable, as they need only an iron ingot.

entries.name: Note Block
facts: It plays on attack, on redstone power, or when used.
It needs air or a mob head directly above to make sound.
Each instrument has 25 pitches, then it wraps around.
entries.tip: Press F3 while looking at one to read its note value from 0 to 24.

entries.name: Jukebox
facts: A playing jukebox outputs a redstone signal of strength 15.
Allays dance within 3 blocks of a playing jukebox.
A comparator reads which disc is inside.
entries.tip: A minecart with hopper can pull a disc out before the track ends.

entries.name: Composter
facts: It is ready for bone meal at level 8.
Breaking a composter loses the compost inside.
Leaf litter and wildflowers became compostable in 1.21.5.
entries.tip: Items in the 100% group, like cake, fill a composter fastest.

entries.name: Observer
facts: It emits a power-15 pulse lasting 2 game ticks.
In Java it detects shape updates, like crop growth.
Moving a powered observer turns it off, with no pulse.
entries.tip: Two observers facing each other make a compact fast clock.

entries.name: Piston
facts: A piston can push at most 12 blocks.
In Java, pistons can be powered from one block above.
Blocks needing support are safe on a piston's back.
entries.tip: Put levers and similar support-needing blocks on a piston's back.

entries.name: Hopper
facts: A full block above stops it picking up item entities.
Pistons cannot move hoppers in Java Edition.
Hoppers generate above barrels at trial chamber entrances.
entries.tip: Mine a hopper with a pickaxe, or it drops only its contents.

entries.name: Lectern
facts: Turning a page sends a full-power pulse for 2 ticks.
In Java, punching the lectern retrieves its book.
entries.tip: An axe breaks a lectern fastest, and its book drops too.

entries.name: Grindstone
facts: It does not remove curses or custom names.
It needs no supporting block when placed.
Pale oak planks work in its recipe since 1.21.2.
entries.tip: Put two damaged same-type tools in it for one repaired, unenchanted tool.

entries.name: Smithing Table
facts: Netherite upgrades need a template, diamond gear and an ingot.
Applying a template costs no experience.
It can serve as furnace fuel for 1.5 items.
entries.tip: Upgrades keep the item's enchantments and custom name.

entries.name: Cartography Table
facts: It can clone, zoom out and lock maps.
It generates in cartographer houses and trail ruins.
entries.tip: Zooming out needs an existing map, so make a base map first.

entries.name: Campfire
facts: Its fire never spreads to nearby blocks.
Pistons cannot move or break it.
It cannot be extinguished from its bottom face.
entries.tip: Put one within 5 blocks below a hive with open air to harvest honey calmly.

entries.name: Lantern
facts: It gives off light level 15.
It melts snow within 2 blocks and ice within 3.
A piston destroys a lantern instead of moving it.
entries.tip: Hang a lantern from a chain; the two connect seamlessly.

entries.name: Glowstone
facts: It gives off light level 15, the maximum.
Redstone power passes up through it but not down.
Monsters cannot spawn on it.
entries.tip: A powered dispenser holding glowstone can charge a respawn anchor.

entries.name: Sea Lantern
facts: It gives off light level 15.
Monsters cannot spawn on it in Java.
Without Silk Touch it drops 2 to 3 prismarine crystals.
entries.tip: Use Silk Touch to keep the sea lantern block itself.

entries.name: Honey Block
facts: It does not carry redstone signals.
Landing on it cuts fall damage by four-fifths.
It slows walking noticeably.
entries.tip: Slide down a honey block wall to descend slowly and avoid fall damage.

entries.name: Tinted Glass
facts: It blocks light and beacon beams completely.
Mobs cannot spawn on top of it.
It drops itself when broken by any means.
entries.tip: No Silk Touch needed: tinted glass always drops when broken.

entries.name: Lightning Rod
facts: A rod topping its column diverts strikes within 128 blocks.
A struck rod emits a power-15 pulse for 8 ticks.
Any non-air block above the rod blocks diversion.
entries.tip: Keep flammable blocks away from the rod; strikes can ignite nearby blocks.

entries.name: Target
facts: Arrows and tridents keep it powered for 20 ticks.
Most other projectiles keep it powered for 8 ticks.
Targets are flammable and burn from lava.
entries.tip: A hoe breaks a target fastest.

entries.name: Daylight Detector
facts: Pistons cannot move it.
Its output refreshes once per second.
A non-inverted one gives no signal in the Nether or End.
entries.tip: Use the inverted mode with a redstone lamp for automatic night lighting.

entries.name: Redstone Lamp
facts: It lights instantly but takes 4 ticks to turn off.
A lit lamp gives off light level 15.
A redstone torch does not power the lamp it is attached to.
entries.tip: Power a lamp with a redstone block, repeater, or a torch under a solid block.

entries.name: Command Block
facts: It only runs when the command_blocks_work game rule is on.
Java command blocks run at operator level 2.
Commands like /stop and /op cannot run in them.
entries.tip: Ctrl plus pick block copies a command block's command and settings.

entries.name: Brewing Stand
facts: In Java it emits light level 1.
Pistons cannot push it in Java Edition.
Since 1.21.4 it drops when broken with any tool.
entries.tip: Hoppers can feed it: from above for ingredients, from the side for bottles and fuel.

entries.name: Dispenser
facts: Pistons cannot move dispensers in Java Edition.
It waits 4 ticks after activation and ignores input meanwhile.
Each activation ejects one item from a random slot.
entries.tip: It fires only on a rising signal edge, so use a clock for repeated shots.

entries.name: Dropper
facts: Pistons cannot move droppers in Java Edition.
It waits 4 ticks after activation and ignores input meanwhile.
Java droppers can be triggered by quasi-connectivity.
entries.tip: One pulse ejects only one item, so use a clock to move several.

entries.name: Loom
facts: It is the shepherd villager's job site block.
Any tool breaks it, and it always drops itself.
It can burn as furnace fuel for 1.5 items.
entries.tip: An axe breaks a loom fastest.

entries.name: Respawn Anchor
facts: Hoglins avoid respawn anchors, even uncharged ones.
Since 1.21.2, entering an End exit portal uses no charge.
The ender dragon cannot destroy it.
entries.tip: Charge it with glowstone blocks, and mine it with a diamond pickaxe or better.

entries.name: Block of Amethyst
facts: Mining it with any pickaxe drops the block; other tools drop nothing.
Next to a sculk sensor it re-emits vibrations, so chains can relay signals.
Hit by a projectile, it rings louder than it does under ordinary interaction.
entries.tip: Bring a wooden pickaxe or better; it is required to mine this block.

entries.name: Budding Amethyst
facts: Each growth attempt has a 20% chance per side; full growth averages about 2h16m.
Pistons destroy it, and sticky pistons or slime/honey blocks cannot pull it.
It cannot be obtained in Survival; breaking it drops nothing, even with Silk Touch.
entries.tip: Buds only grow when attached directly to a budding amethyst block.

entries.name: Calcite
facts: It generates in amethyst geodes between the smooth basalt and amethyst layers.
Real-world calcite is the most stable form of calcium carbonate.
Bare-handed breaking takes 13.75 seconds in Java Edition.
entries.tip: Mine it with any pickaxe, or it will not drop as an item.

entries.name: Deepslate
facts: Hardness is 3, so it takes much longer to mine than regular stone.
It makes up most solid blocks below Y=0 and is common in ancient cities.
Without Silk Touch it drops cobbled deepslate instead of itself.
entries.tip: Smelt cobbled deepslate in a furnace to turn it back into deepslate.

entries.name: Tuff
facts: It generates in blobs in the Overworld between Y=-64 and Y=0, in all biomes.
Ores generating inside tuff turn into deepslate variants below Y=0.
It also appears in trial chamber corridors and supply chests.
entries.tip: Mine it with a pickaxe; without one it drops nothing.

entries.name: Dripstone Block
facts: Hardness is 1.5 and blast resistance is 1; it needs a pickaxe to drop.
Four pointed dripstone craft into one dripstone block.
Mason villagers sell it, which makes it renewable.
entries.tip: Put water above a stalactite on a dripstone block to make it grow slowly.

entries.name: Moss Block
facts: It generates on floors and ceilings in lush caves.
Composting one has a 65% chance to raise the compost level.
Sniffer eggs hatch faster when placed on moss blocks.
entries.tip: Break moss blocks with a hoe; it is the fastest tool.

entries.name: Sculk Sensor
facts: It detects vibrations within an 8-block spherical radius.
After a signal it stays active for 30 game ticks (1.5 seconds).
It generates naturally in the deep dark and in ancient cities.
entries.tip: Sneak near a sensor; sneaking stops movement from creating vibrations.

entries.name: Sculk Shrieker
facts: It generates in the deep dark, far more often in ancient cities.
Player-placed or catalyst-spawned shriekers cannot summon wardens or cause Darkness.
Mined without Silk Touch, it drops 5 experience instead of the block.
entries.tip: Break it with a hoe, the fastest tool for it.

entries.name: Sculk Catalyst
facts: It blooms when a living entity dies within 8 blocks in Java Edition.
A warden drops one on death, the only renewable source.
It emits light level 6.
entries.tip: Use a hoe to mine it, and Silk Touch if you want the block itself.

entries.name: Mangrove Roots
facts: Hardness and blast resistance are both 0.7.
They can be waterlogged, and are flammable, catching fire from lava.
In a composter they have a 30% chance to add a compost level.
entries.tip: You can break roots by hand, but an axe is quickest.

entries.name: Block of Bamboo
facts: Hardness and blast resistance are both 2.
It cannot be crafted back into bamboo or smelted into charcoal.
As furnace fuel one block smelts 1.5 items.
entries.tip: Craft it into planks first: two planks as fuel smelt 3 items, double the block.

entries.name: Ancient Debris
facts: It generates in the Nether only where not exposed to air, replacing netherrack, basalt or blackstone.
Taking out smelted netherite scrap grants 2 experience points.
It was added in Java Edition 1.16 snapshot 20w06a.
entries.tip: Mine it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe; other tools drop nothing.

entries.name: Crying Obsidian
facts: Piglin bartering is its only renewable source, about 8.5% chance for 1-3 blocks.
In ruined portals each obsidian block has a 15% chance to be crying obsidian.
It is crafted with glowstone into a respawn anchor.
entries.tip: Use a diamond or netherite pickaxe; weaker tools are slow and drop nothing.

entries.name: Soul Sand
facts: Without Soul Speed boots it slows movement by about 41.9%.
Four soul sand in a T with three wither skeleton skulls summon a wither.
Solid cover thicker than half a block removes its slowing effect.
entries.tip: Cover soul sand with a solid block thicker than half a block to walk normally.

entries.name: Magma Block
facts: It emits light level 3.
Underwater it makes a downward bubble column that pulls entities down.
A pickaxe is required for it to drop anything.
entries.tip: Sneak while standing on a magma block to avoid its burning damage.

entries.name: Blue Ice
facts: One block needs 81 ice, crafted via packed ice.
Its slipperiness is 0.989, above ice and packed ice at 0.98.
Boats reach about 72.7 m/s on it versus 40 m/s on ice.
entries.tip: Place blue ice under a water current to speed up items travelling in it.

entries.name: Packed Ice
facts: Unlike regular ice, it does not melt near light sources.
Nine ice craft one packed ice, making it renewable.
It never turns into water when broken, and drops nothing without Silk Touch.
entries.tip: A pickaxe is the fastest tool for breaking it.

entries.name: End Stone
facts: Its blast resistance is 9, three more than ordinary stone.
Endermen cannot pick it up and the ender dragon cannot destroy it.
It is the only block chorus flowers can be planted on.
entries.tip: Mine it with a pickaxe; by hand it drops nothing.

entries.name: Chorus Flower
facts: It drops as an item only when broken directly or hit by a projectile.
Bone meal has no effect on its growth.
It grows regardless of light level when planted on end stone.
entries.tip: A flower that stopped growing at age 5 can be harvested and replanted to reset it.

entries.name: Bedrock
facts: Its hardness is -1, so it cannot be broken, and blast resistance is 3,600,000.
In Survival it is only available via Creative, pick block, or commands.
Mobs cannot spawn on it.
entries.tip: A bedrock setup like the exit portal's can securely trap a wither in Java Edition.

entries.name: Monster Spawner
facts: Survival players cannot obtain one, even with Silk Touch.
A player within a 16-block spherical radius of its center activates it.
Each cycle attempts 4 mobs, then waits 10 to 39.95 seconds.
entries.tip: For dark-only spawners, a torch on any side or top disables the whole spawning volume.

entries.name: Sponge
facts: Sponges can only be found in ocean monuments.
A wet sponge placed in the Nether dries instantly into a normal sponge.
It absorbs water up to 6 blocks away but no more than 118 water blocks.
entries.tip: Mine sponges with a hoe; it breaks them faster than other tools.

entries.name: Cobweb
facts: Players move at roughly 25% of normal speed while touching one.
Since 1.21, entities with Weaving spawn 2-3 cobwebs on death, making it renewable.
They generate in mineshafts, strongholds, trial chambers and more.
entries.tip: Break cobwebs with shears; they are quickest and drop the cobweb itself.

entries.name: Mud Bricks
facts: They are crafted from 4 packed mud.
They generate naturally in trail ruins, added in 1.20.
They were announced at Minecraft Live 2021.
entries.tip: Mine them with a pickaxe; any other tool drops nothing.

entries.name: Block of Copper
facts: Unwaxed copper has four oxidation stages, counting the initial state.
A non-oxidized block equals nine copper ingots.
It needs at least a stone pickaxe to drop anything.
entries.tip: Use a stonecutter for slabs and stairs; it yields four times as many as crafting would.

entries.name: Block of Diamond
facts: It equals nine diamonds.
It generates in woodland mansion obsidian and lava rooms.
It needs an iron pickaxe or better to mine.
entries.tip: A 3x3 of diamond blocks under a beacon powers it; layers can mix in other mineral blocks.

entries.name: Block of Netherite
facts: It is made from nine netherite ingots.
Its blast resistance is 1,200, the same as obsidian.
Its item form is immune to fire and lava, but a cactus can destroy it.
entries.tip: Unlike obsidian, pistons can push netherite blocks, handy in redstone builds.

entries.name: Shroomlight
facts: It emits light level 15, the highest in the game.
It generates near the top of huge crimson and warped fungi.
Since 20w12a it is renewable and no longer burns from lava.
entries.tip: Break shroomlights with a hoe, the fastest tool for them.

entries.name: Nether Wart Block
facts: It cannot be crafted back into nether wart.
It generates in huge crimson fungi in crimson forests.
Composting one has an 85% chance to raise the compost level.
entries.tip: A hoe is the fastest way to break it.

entries.name: Diamond
facts: Diamond ore is found at Y 15 or lower, most commonly between -50 and -64.
Diamonds are needed for diamond tools, armor and enchanting tables.
entries.tip: Fortune III on an iron or better pickaxe can drop up to 4 diamonds per ore.

entries.name: Ender Pearl
facts: Pearls first appeared alongside endermen, with no use at first.
Teleporting arrived in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 2, when stacks were cut to 16.
They became an ingredient for eyes of ender in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3.
entries.tip: Throwing a pearl just before landing replaces fall damage with the pearl's damage.

entries.name: Eye of Ender
facts: Each throw has a 20% chance of shattering the eye.
An eye can be placed in an End portal frame or thrown to locate a stronghold.
entries.tip: Eyes only locate strongholds in the Overworld; they do nothing in the Nether or End.

entries.name: Golden Apple
facts: At first golden apples healed fully and were the best food in the game.
Apples were unobtainable then, so golden apples were too.
entries.tip: Unlike most foods, a golden apple can be eaten with a full hunger bar.

entries.name: Elytra
facts: Java elytra have 432 durability, about 7 minutes 12 seconds of gliding.
Phantom membrane replaced leather for anvil repairs in 1.13.
entries.tip: For a long cruise, aim at the horizon at the altitude limit of your glide.

entries.name: Compass
facts: Librarian villagers started selling compasses in 1.3.1 (12w21a).
Lodestone compasses came in 1.16 along with lodestones.
entries.tip: Craft a lodestone compass to point at a specific lodestone block.

entries.name: Recovery Compass
facts: It is crafted from an echo shard and a compass.
In 1.21.2 its rarity was changed from Common to Uncommon.
entries.tip: It is useless in Hardcore mode, since players there cannot respawn.

entries.name: Clock
facts: Librarians started selling clocks in 1.3.1, making them renewable.
Shipwreck map rooms can contain clocks since 1.13.
entries.tip: You can sleep a few seconds after the clock shows exactly dusk.

entries.name: Spyglass
facts: It was revealed at Minecraft Live 2020 under the name telescope.
Zoom is 1/10 of your field of view, so 70 degrees becomes 7.
entries.tip: Press F1 while zoomed to hide the scope overlay in Java Edition.

entries.name: Totem of Undying
facts: It became renewable in 1.14 when evokers began appearing in raids.
Evokers always drop one totem, and Looting does not affect it.
entries.tip: The totem must be held in a hand to work; one in the hotbar does nothing.

entries.name: Trident
facts: Tridents were unobtainable in Survival until drowned arrived.
Durability was lowered from 251 to 250 in snapshot 18w30b.
entries.tip: A Loyalty trident acts as a Nether bow substitute; it returns even from lava.

entries.name: Nether Star
facts: Nether stars are dropped by the wither.
Dropped stars became immune to explosions in 1.4.6 (12w49a).
entries.tip: A dropped Nether star despawns after 10 minutes, so grab it promptly.

entries.name: Heart of the Sea
facts: Every buried treasure chest holds exactly one.
Its rarity was changed from Common to Uncommon in 18w21a.
entries.tip: Buried treasure maps with a red X are found in ocean ruins and shipwrecks.

entries.name: Echo Shard
facts: Echo shards are found only in ancient city chests, 1 to 3 per chest.
Their only use is crafting recovery compasses.
entries.tip: Combine one echo shard with a compass to craft a recovery compass.

entries.name: Bundle
facts: Bundles needed an experimental data pack until snapshot 24w39a (1.21.2).
In 24w33a the recipe became one string plus one leather.
entries.tip: Right-click a bundle with an empty cursor to take out the last item added.

entries.name: Brush
facts: Brushes first appeared in snapshot 23w07a behind an experimental pack.
Brushing a single suspicious block takes 96 game ticks, or 4.8 seconds.
entries.tip: Keep brushing without interruption, or the block gradually reverts.

entries.name: Lead
facts: Leads were added in snapshot 13w16a, originally called leashes.
They can tether horses, pigs, cows, chickens, sheep and mooshrooms.
entries.tip: Sneak while using a fence on a leashed mob to tie it to the fence.

entries.name: Name Tag
facts: Name tags were first found in dungeon chests.
Fishing made them renewable in 1.7.2 (13w36a).
entries.tip: Rename a full stack of tags at once; it costs 1 experience level per stack.

entries.name: Firework Rocket
facts: Rockets arrived in snapshot 12w49a.
At first they could not be taken from the Creative inventory.
entries.tip: A rocket without a firework star has no explosion, so a crossbow shot does no damage.

entries.name: Blaze Rod
facts: Blaze rods became usable for blaze powder in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 2.
They became a brewing stand ingredient in Prerelease 3.
entries.tip: Blazes drop rods only when killed by a player or a tamed wolf.

entries.name: Honeycomb
facts: Honeycomb arrived in snapshot 19w34a, used to craft beehives.
Trial chamber chests can hold it since snapshot 23w45a.
entries.tip: Put a campfire under a hive before shearing so the bees stay calm.

entries.name: Glow Berries
facts: They arrived in snapshot 21w05a together with cave vines.
Eating one restores 2 hunger points; foxes can be bred with them.
entries.tip: Right-click a berry-bearing cave vine to pick berries without breaking it.

entries.name: Sweet Berries
facts: They arrived in snapshot 18w49a along with sweet berry bushes.
Foxes could be bred with them from 19w07a.
entries.tip: Bone meal on a sweet berry bush advances its growth by one stage.

entries.name: Cookie
facts: Cookies originally healed 1 HP and stacked to 8.
Stack size became 64 in Beta 1.8 Pre-release.
entries.tip: Cookies are a good compost input: each has an 85% chance to raise the level.

entries.name: Amethyst Shard
facts: A fully grown amethyst cluster drops 4 shards.
Shards can duplicate an allay near an active jukebox, with a 5-minute cooldown.
entries.tip: Mine clusters without Silk Touch or Fortune to get the 4 shards.

entries.name: Netherite Ingot
facts: Ingots were added in snapshot 20w06a.
The ingot itself is immune to being destroyed by fire and lava.
entries.tip: A smithing table upgrades diamond gear using an ingot and an upgrade template.

entries.name: Phantom Membrane
facts: Tamed cats can bring membranes as gifts since 1.14.
Its texture was changed in snapshot 19w08a.
entries.tip: One membrane in an anvil restores 25% of an elytra's durability, keeping enchantments.

entries.name: Wind Charge
facts: Wind charges debuted in snapshot 23w45a under an experimental pack.
They can be crafted from breeze rods since 24w11a.
entries.tip: Wind charges have a 0.5 second cooldown that covers all stacks in your inventory.

entries.name: Mace
facts: Maces first appeared in snapshot 24w11a.
Durability was raised from 250 to 500 in 24w18a.
entries.tip: Repair a mace in an anvil with a breeze rod for 25% durability; enchantments stay.

entries.name: Fishing Rod
facts: At first rods had no function and were held backward.
Rods could catch fish from any water in Alpha 1.2.0, with 64 durability.
entries.tip: A carrot on a stick needs the fishing rod diagonally above the carrot.

entries.name: Creeper
facts: Its fuse lasts 30 ticks (1.5 seconds) once it is within 3 blocks of you.
Lightning within 4 blocks charges it, raising explosion power from 3 to 6.
Cats and ocelots scare creepers away within 6 blocks.
entries.tip: Break line of sight during the fuse and the explosion is cancelled.

entries.name: Enderman
facts: It is the only mob that spawns naturally in all three dimensions.
Looking at its eyes within 64 blocks for 5 ticks provokes it.
Rain, water and splash water bottles hurt it.
entries.tip: Wear a carved pumpkin so looking at endermen will not anger them.

entries.name: Axolotl
facts: Blue axolotls do not spawn naturally; babies have a 1/1200 chance of being blue.
Hurt underwater, it may play dead for 10 seconds and gain Regeneration I.
Out of water with no deep water nearby, it dies after 5 minutes.
entries.tip: Feed a baby a bucket of tropical fish; each use cuts 10% of its remaining growth time.

entries.name: Allay
facts: It spawns only in pillager outpost cages and woodland mansion cells, in groups of 1-3.
It collects dropped items matching the one you gave it, searching within 32 blocks.
Giving an amethyst shard to a dancing allay duplicates it.
entries.tip: Give it an item, then drop more of that item nearby and it will gather them for you.

entries.name: Warden
facts: It appears after a player triggers sculk shriekers four times.
Its sonic boom ignores armor and shields and passes through blocks.
It always drops one sculk catalyst when killed.
entries.tip: Sneaking avoids vibration detection, but it can still smell you, so keep your distance.

entries.name: Bee
facts: A bee that stings loses its stinger and dies about a minute later.
Each hive holds up to 3 bees and needs honey level 5 to harvest.
It is the only arthropod mob that can spawn on Peaceful difficulty.
entries.tip: Put a campfire under a hive before harvesting so the bees stay calm.

entries.name: Fox
facts: Red foxes live in taigas; snow foxes live in snowy taigas and groves.
Foxes can fall 5 blocks before taking damage, versus 3 for most mobs.
They hunt fish in water and will swim to do it.
entries.tip: Sneak toward a fox; it will not flee until you are right next to it.

entries.name: Frog
facts: Frogs come in temperate, warm and cold variants, set by biome.
Eating a magma cube makes a frog drop a froglight matching its variant.
Frogs can jump up to 8 blocks high.
entries.tip: Hold a slimeball within 6 blocks to lure frogs, then feed two to breed them.

entries.name: Goat
facts: About 2% of goats are screaming goats, with different sounds and more ramming.
Ramming stone, logs or packed ice can knock off a horn, dropping a goat horn.
An adult goat can be milked with a bucket.
entries.tip: Hold wheat near a goat that is winding up a ram and it will walk to you instead.

entries.name: Iron Golem
facts: It is built from four iron blocks in a T shape topped with a carved pumpkin.
An iron ingot heals it by 25 HP.
It cracks visibly as it takes damage.
entries.tip: Stand on a three-block pillar to hit golems without being reached.

entries.name: Snow Golem
facts: It is made from two snow blocks and a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern.
Its snowballs do no damage except to blazes, but they knock mobs back.
Rain, water and hot biomes damage it.
entries.tip: Fire Resistance lets a snow golem survive in deserts and other hot biomes.

entries.name: Villager
facts: A baby villager becomes an adult after 20 minutes.
Breeding needs 12 nutrition points; bread counts for 4, carrots and potatoes for 1.
Nitwits cannot trade or take a profession.
entries.tip: Once you trade with a villager, its profession is locked for good.

entries.name: Wandering Trader
facts: Each trader offers nine trades.
It arrives with two leashed trader llamas.
In Java, it despawns after 48,000 ticks nearby; name tags do not stop this.
entries.tip: A trader summoned by egg or command has a DespawnDelay of 0, so it stays put.

entries.name: Wolf
facts: Each bone has a 1/3 chance of taming a wild wolf.
Tamed wolves have 40 HP; wild ones have 8 HP.
There are 9 wolf variants, each tied to a biome.
entries.tip: Feed a hurt tamed wolf cooked porkchop to restore 16 HP per item.

entries.name: Panda
facts: Pandas have seven personalities, with brown the rarest at about 1.6%.
Lazy pandas are the slowest land mob in the game.
Since 24w21a they panic only from cactus, freezing, fire and lightning damage.
entries.tip: To breed pandas, keep at least one bamboo plant within a 7x7x3 area.

entries.name: Parrot
facts: Parrots cannot breed, and baby parrots do not exist.
They imitate nearby mobs' idle sounds within 20 blocks.
Seeds tame them with a 1/10 chance each; cookies kill them.
entries.tip: Bring plenty of seeds, since each has only a 1/10 chance to tame a parrot.

entries.name: Sniffer
facts: Sniffers cannot spawn naturally and only come from hatched eggs.
They dig up torchflower seeds or pitcher pods with equal chance.
A snifflet takes 40 minutes to grow up, twice as long as most babies.
entries.tip: Place sniffer eggs on moss blocks to hatch them in 10 minutes instead of 20.

entries.name: Camel
facts: One camel spawns in the center of each non-abandoned desert village.
Two players can ride one camel at once.
Camels can fall 6 blocks safely, versus 3 for most mobs.
entries.tip: Feed a baby camel cactus to shave 10 seconds off its remaining growth time.

entries.name: Ender Dragon
facts: It has 200 HP but takes about 75% less damage unless hit on the head.
The first defeat drops 12,000 XP.
Respawning it needs four End crystals around the exit portal.
entries.tip: Aim for the head; other hitboxes take heavy damage reduction.

entries.name: Wither
facts: It is the only source of nether stars, needed for beacons.
It is the only mob that can destroy obsidian.
Below half health it gains armor that blocks arrows.
entries.tip: Summon it far from your base; its spawn explosion wrecks nearby blocks.

entries.name: Ghast
facts: Ghasts are the only source of ghast tears.
A fireball deflected back into a ghast kills it instantly.
Once it targets you, it fires a fireball every 3 seconds.
entries.tip: Hit its fireball back from a distance to kill it in one shot.

entries.name: Strider
facts: Striders spawn in groups of 2 to 4 on lava in all Nether biomes.
Lava does not hurt them and they walk on top of it.
Out of lava they turn purple, shiver and slow down.
entries.tip: Face a solid block before dismounting so you do not land in lava.

entries.name: Turtle
facts: Turtles are the only source of turtle scutes, dropped by growing babies.
After breeding, a Java turtle lays 1-4 eggs and has a 5-minute cooldown.
Babies take 20 minutes to grow up.
entries.tip: Feed baby turtles seagrass; each use cuts 10% of their remaining growth time.

entries.name: Glow Squid
facts: It is the only source of glow ink sacs.
It won the 2020 mob vote.
Java spawns them in groups of 4 to 6.
entries.tip: Use Looting III to raise the average ink sac yield from 2 to 3.5 per kill.

entries.name: Slime
facts: A killed large slime splits into two to four medium slimes.
About one in ten chunks is a slime chunk, decided by the world seed.
Slimes ignore lava and cactus because they move straight at their target.
entries.tip: Slimes need a clear 2.08-block cube of space to spawn; any solid block blocks them.

entries.name: Shulker
facts: Shulkers are found only in End cities.
They are the only source of shulker shells, used for shulker boxes.
Their bullets apply Levitation for 10 seconds in Java Edition.
entries.tip: Raise a shield to block shulker bullets and avoid Levitation.

entries.name: Cherry Grove
facts: Villages cannot generate here, but pillager outposts can.
Sugar cane and pumpkin patches do not generate in it in Java.
Dripstone caves and the deep dark are common beneath it.
entries.tip: Look at lower plains beside a grove if you want a nearby village.

entries.name: Deep Dark
facts: It is the only biome where ancient cities can generate.
Regular hostile mobs do not spawn; only the warden can appear.
It is the only Overworld biome without lava lakes.
entries.tip: Bone meal grows flowers here as in plains, so you can plant tulips underground.

entries.name: Lush Caves
facts: It is the only biome where axolotls spawn.
It generates most often under humid biomes like dark forests and old growth taigas.
Java Edition lush caves have rain, unlike Bedrock's arid ones.
entries.tip: Azalea trees on the surface hint that a lush cave lies below.

entries.name: Mushroom Fields
facts: Mushroom fields always generate as islands surrounded by deep ocean.
Mooshrooms spawn naturally only here.
It covers about 0.14% of the Overworld, a very rare surface biome.
entries.tip: Natural hostile mobs skip its surface, but spawners and raids still work.
